Subject: Sudden spike in latency & 5xx errors - production

Hi Kimberly,

We started seeing a large uptick in request latency and a cascade of 5xx errors hitting our live inference route at ~08:45 PDT. User-facing timeouts and retries are now causing substantial backpressure in our queueing layer — we have multiple partners reporting failed requests.

Quick facts:
- Error rate from 08:45-09:05: ~12% 5xx on /v1/generate
- Median latency jumped from 220ms to ~1.6s
- Peak concurrency ~2.5x normal

Can you confirm whether this is an infrastructure capacity issue or a model/serving regression? We need a triage path and an ETA for mitigation.

Thanks,
Mateo
CTO, ArborHealth

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com

Date: 2027-09-18T09:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fw: Sudden spike in latency & 5xx errors - production

On bridge now. Initial triage:
- No recent deploys to redwood-1b-prod in the last 6 hrs.
- Multiple worker nodes reporting elevated GPU memory pressure; seeing frequent cache-miss rebuilds for KV cache.
- One host (gpu-34) rebooted at 08:49 due to nvlink timeout; autoscaler replaced it but backlog spiked while new instances warmed the KV cache.
- Heap dumps captured from two unlucky workers; attaching pointers.

Short term mitigation performed (09:22):
- Warmed additional instances in the same region and pinned more capacity to ArborHealth's pool.
- Reduced max prefix caching to force less aggressive KV rebuilds (avoids large transient spikes).

Next: collect full heap dumps and check whether a quantized kernel regression is causing oversized allocations. Marcus will follow up in 30 min.

Marcus Lin
SRE Manager

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com

Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fw: Sudden spike in latency & 5xx errors - production

Update from routing & customer config:
- ArborHealth traffic is routed to us in us-west-2 primarily; no recent routing changes on their account.
- Their SLA plan has dedicated reserved capacity (30 GPUs) but their burst policy allows automatic warm-up for +10 GPUs. The warm-up delay explains part of the ~20–30s tail.
- They had an unusually large batch job scheduled by their internal analytics team which drove concurrency up by ~2.6x starting ~08:42. We did not receive a pre-warm signal.

Recommendation: keep pinned extra nodes (already done), and ask partner to gate scheduled batch jobs with pre-warm or set a lower concurrency cap until we complete full postmortem.

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: Mateo Silva <mateo@arborhealth.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-18T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: ArborHealth incident — immediate status & short-term mitigations

Mateo — thanks for flagging this. Quick status for external partners: 

What we saw: increased concurrency from a scheduled analytics run caused GPU memory pressure and KV cache rebuilds; one host rebooted and autoscaler warm-up added transient backlog. That produced higher latency and a short window of 5xxs.

What we’ve done (completed):
- Added warm instances and pinned capacity to your pool.
- Reduced aggressive KV prefetch to limit transient memory spikes.
- Applied temporary concurrency cap you can opt into (recommended).

What we suggest next (ETA):
- We will run targeted kernel checks and analyze heap dumps (Marcus) — ETA 6 hours.
- If we find a kernel/quantization regression we will provide a hotfix or targeted rollback plan — ETA 12–24 hours.
- We will schedule a joint runbook review and gating for scheduled batch jobs to prevent recurrence.

I will keep you posted; Kim and Laura are on the exec path if you need a leadership-level update.

— Priyom
Solutions Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-18T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity & rollback options — follow-up

Following the morning work, we completed deeper checks:
- Autoscaler logs show warm-up latency for new GPU instances of ~45–70s due to KV bootstrapping.
- No evidence yet of a wide kernel regression across other customers. The impact appears amplified for accounts with high prefix reuse (ArborHealth).

Options for immediate customer protection:
1) Keep pinned + manual scale till we ship a kernel fix (costly but fast).
2) Force-fallback to a smaller model variant with lower memory footprint (possible 8–12% QA delta).
3) Apply short-term customer-side concurrency caps and gate scheduled batches (lowest cost, requires coordination).

Recommend: combination of 1 + 3 for the next 24 hours while Marcus completes deep analysis. I’ll prepare a cost estimate for option 1 if Execs approve.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Infrastructure Operations

Thanks again for the patience while we worked through this. This thread captures the full triage timeline — key points below for your execs: 

Executive summary (as of 21:00 PDT, 09/19):

- Impact: elevated latencies and ~10–12% 5xx window during the incident peak.
- Mitigation completed: pinned additional capacity to ArborHealth pool, reduced aggressive KV prefetch, applied a recommended concurrency cap, and warmed replacement instances.

Immediate next steps (24h):
- Marcus: complete heap-dump analysis and kernel regression check — deliverable: technical findings w/ proposed fix (ETA: +6 hrs).
- Vivek: standby cost estimate for manual capacity for 24–48 hrs (if you want us to continue pinned capacity) — deliverable: cost + approval path (ETA: +3 hrs).
- Priyom & Laura: schedule a joint runbook review and gating policy for scheduled batch jobs; propose guardrails (ETA: 24–48 hrs).

If you would like a short leadership-to-leadership update call, we can schedule a 15-min sync this evening or tomorrow morning. Please tell us preferred time.

We’ve attached a short runbook excerpt and the metrics summary we used for triage.

Sincerely,

Kimberly Park
